note: Run in an environment with (a) the hms-acp-incident-mcp server built & connected and (b) git access to the private HumanSoftTH repos — e.g. Claude Code on your machine. Eval 4 deliberately runs WITHOUT the MCP to test the precondition path. Assertions are checked by hand or by inspecting the working tree / branches.

evals.prompt: มี incident อะไรที่ยังไม่เสร็จบ้างเดือนนี้
evals.expected_output: Skill confirms the incident MCP is connected, lists this-month not-done incidents (id/title/status, platform if available) in Thai, then STOPS and asks which one to work on. It must NOT diagnose or touch any repo or card yet.

assertions.text: Incidents are pulled via hms-acp-incident-mcp (a listing tool is actually called), not invented.
Scope defaults to the current month, resolved from today's date; terminal/done statuses are excluded.
The list is presented in Thai and is scannable (id, title, status at minimum).
The skill stops and asks which incident — no diagnosis, no code reading, no card writes in this run.

evals.prompt: เอา INC-<ใส่ id จริง> ตัวนี้แหละ ช่วยดูหน่อยว่าต้องแก้ที่ไหน
evals.expected_output: Skill fetches the incident detail via MCP, routes it to the correct repo(s)/layer (CCS web-ccs / HRS web-hrs / api-server), locates the module and the implicated files, states a code-evidence-backed root cause with confidence, and asks whether to implement the fix — then STOPS. No edits yet.

assertions.text: Incident detail is fetched via the MCP get-detail tool.
Routing conclusion is explicit: which repo(s) AND which layer (FE/BE), with the evidence that placed it there.
Root cause cites concrete file:line evidence from the cloned code, not just a restatement of the card text.
Shared-backend blast radius is called out if the fix would be in api-server (affects both CCS and HRS).
A confidence level is given; if not high, open questions / what-to-check are listed.
The skill asks for permission to fix and STOPS — it does not start editing.

evals.prompt: ใช่เลย แก้โค้ดให้หน่อย
evals.expected_output: Following a prior diagnosis, the skill creates a fix/<INCIDENT-ID>-<slug> branch in each implicated repo, makes minimal targeted edits, leaves them unpushed in the working tree, summarizes the diff per file in Thai, and drafts a ready-to-paste incident-update message. It must NOT push, open a PR, or write to the card.

assertions.text: A new branch named fix/<incident-id>-<slug> is created in each implicated repo.
Edits are minimal and scoped to the root cause — no unrelated refactors/renames.
NOTHING is pushed and no PR is opened (verify: no remote branch, no PR); changes remain local.
No MCP card-write tool is called; instead a Thai update message is drafted as text for the user to paste.
A per-file diff/summary is presented in Thai and the closing note states the branch is local and unpushed.

evals.prompt: ดู incident เดือนนี้ให้หน่อย
evals.expected_output: With hms-acp-incident-mcp NOT connected, the skill detects the missing server and stops gracefully — explaining in Thai that the MCP has a spec but must be built and connected first. It must not invent incidents or silently substitute another source.

assertions.text: The skill notices the incident MCP is not connected before trying to list.
It explains in Thai that the server needs to be built from its spec and connected, and stops.
It does NOT fabricate incidents or fall back to Jira/another source without being asked.
